display_name: Sher Shah Suri & Puran Mal of Raisen
one_line: Afghan emperor Sher Shah Suri and Rajput chief Puran Mal at the fraught 1543 siege and massacre of Raisen.

appearance.age_look: Sher Shah appears as a wiry, commanding man in his late 40s; Puran Mal as a broad-shouldered, battle-hardened Rajput in his early 40s.
appearance.face: Sher Shah has a lean oval face, wheatish to light-brown complexion, sharp hooked nose, neatly trimmed beard and mustache, intense narrow eyes with a calculating gaze, and a calm, authoritative default expression; Puran Mal has a square jaw, medium-brown complexion, thick arched brows, strong straight nose, fuller beard and long mustache, and a proud, stormy expression hinting both defiance and responsibility.
appearance.hair: Sher Shah’s hair is dark brown, short and mostly hidden under a deep green quilted Afghan-style turban wrapped low with a simple gold band at the front; Puran Mal’s hair is black, shoulder-length and slightly wavy, pulled back under a saffron Rajput turban with a forward-curving green cloth fan and a small central metal turban-ornament.
appearance.costume: Sher Shah wears a long, knee-length Persianate jama of muted cream cotton with fine vertical tan stripes, tied diagonally with a narrow brown sash, over loose deep-green churidar-style trousers; his outer layer is a sleeveless dark-red quilted coat (nim-qaba) with simple gold edging, and at his waist a broad leather belt carries a small utility pouch; his footwear is brown leather mojari shoes with modest upturned toes. Puran Mal wears a fitted, long-sleeved, knee-length angarkha of rich off-white cotton with subtle block-printed floral motifs in pale maroon, fastened on the side with cloth ties, over indigo-blue tight churidar trousers; over this he has a sleeveless steel brigandine-style vest with rows of small rivets, worn atop a padded cotton under-layer visible at the shoulders; a thick maroon cloth patka sash wraps his waist with the loose ends hanging to one side, and he wears tan leather boots reaching mid-calf, practical for fort terrain.
appearance.signature: Sher Shah carries at his left side a slightly curved Indo-Afghan talwar with a simple steel hilt and round pommel in a plain dark-brown scabbard, his right hand often resting lightly on the grip; Puran Mal holds a long Rajput spear (bhala) with a leaf-shaped steel head and dark wooden shaft, while a traditional Rajput talwar with a disc pommel hangs sheathed at his left hip from his maroon sash.

ref_desc: Sher Shah Suri has a lean bearded face, dark-green turban, cream striped jama, dark-red quilted coat and brown belt with talwar, while Puran Mal has a square-bearded face, saffron turban, off-white patterned angarkha, steel vest, maroon sash and bhala spear; palette of green, cream, dark red, indigo and saffron.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet showing two standing figures side by side at Raisen Fort: Sher Shah Suri and Puran Mal of Raisen, grounded in 1543 central Indian historical clothing. Sher Shah is lean, with a wheatish complexion, hooked nose, neatly trimmed beard and mustache, and intense narrow eyes; his dark-brown hair is short under a deep-green quilted Afghan-style turban with a simple gold band. He wears a cream cotton knee-length jama with fine tan vertical stripes, tied diagonally by a narrow brown sash, over loose deep-green churidar trousers, and a sleeveless dark-red quilted coat with simple gold edging as his outer layer. A broad leather belt carries a small pouch, and he has brown leather mojari shoes with modest upturned toes. At his left side hangs a plain dark-brown scabbard containing a slightly curved Indo-Afghan talwar with a simple steel hilt and round pommel, his right hand resting lightly on the grip. Beside him stands Puran Mal, broad-shouldered with a square jaw, medium-brown complexion, thick brows, straight nose, fuller beard and long mustache, and a proud, stormy expression. His black shoulder-length hair is pulled back under a saffron Rajput turban with a green cloth fan and a small central metal ornament. He wears a fitted off-white cotton angarkha with subtle pale-maroon floral block prints, over indigo-blue tight churidar trousers, topped by a sleeveless steel brigandine-style vest with visible rows of rivets and a padded cotton under-layer at the shoulders. A thick maroon cloth patka sash wraps his waist, with ends hanging to one side, and he has tan leather mid-calf boots. He holds a long Rajput bhala spear with a leaf-shaped steel head and dark wooden shaft, while a traditional Rajput talwar with disc pommel hangs sheathed at his left hip from the maroon sash. Use a palette dominated by deep green, cream, dark red, indigo blue and saffron, and keep both characters fully clothed, dignified, and consistent with this exact described face, hair, costume and weapons.
